findings.title: Slökkva á 1984 vegna netárásar
findings.summary_md: RÚV reports that the managers of Icelandic hosting company 1984 decided on 20 November to temporarily stop all services after a large and serious cyberattack on the company's IT infrastructure. A joint notice from 1984 and CERT-IS says the scope is still under investigation and that initial findings point to a well-organised, technically advanced attack. DNS and email are expected to return quickly and will operate under special monitoring, while the company gave no date for full restoration. The shutdown is described as a safety step to limit further impact, preserve the investigation and prevent services being restored before their security is verified.

findings.title: 1984 ehf. stöðvar nethýsingarþjónustu eftir netárás
findings.summary_md: Vísir Business reports that 1984 ehf stopped its hosting service after a cyberattack. Its summary of the initial investigation says the attack was well organised and technically advanced; the article was published at 11:15 Icelandic time, which is UTC.

findings.title: Mjög alvarleg tölvuárás frá fjársterkum aðilum
findings.summary_md: RÚV quotes 1984 managing director Mörður Áslaugarson saying the attack was extremely serious, clearly backed by well-funded actors and carried out at a speed he had not heard of before. The company, which hosts a large proportion of Icelandic websites, closed every service to protect customers. He said the complete shutdown would be brief, with email and DNS coming back first and other services restored gradually only once data and customer security were confirmed, but he gave no full restoration date.
